summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a long history of recurrent pancreatitis was readmitted due to a flare triggered by attempting to eat solid food shortly after a prior discharge. She presented with severe epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, and pain control using a Dilaudid PCA initially, then transitioned to oral hydromorphone. TPN was initiated for nutritional support. An endoscopic ultrasound showed no pancreatic mass, and MRCP revealed only chronic changes. A non-occlusive thrombus was detected near the left PICC line, prompting its removal and placement of a new PICC in the right arm. Estrogen therapy with Premarin was discontinued due to thrombosis risk. She improved clinically, with pain control and tolerance of oral medications, and was discharged home with visiting nurse support for PICC and TPN management, along with follow-up plans.
